summary:
We are developing an educational mini-game designed for children aged 7 to 14. While the project is currently a work in progress and not yet fully completed, its core concept integrates learning directly into gameplay through interactive tasks and challenges where players discover interesting and useful facts as they progress.

Our game addresses the common challenge of low student engagement and lack of motivation in traditional education. By turning studying into an exciting adventure, it replaces passive memorization with active curiosity. This approach is important because it helps children build a lifelong love for learning, making education both effective and enjoyable from an early age.
details:
We developed an interactive web-based educational mini-game using HTML (alongside CSS/JavaScript). In the current beta version, the player performs tasks that simulate real astronaut duties on a space station, such as cleaning solar panels and repairing electronics. In the future, we plan to add more global quests, including collecting soil and ice samples from the Martian surface, repairing a Mars rover, and studying celestial bodies in the night sky.

Benefits & Intended Impact

The project makes learning engaging and accessible, helping children gain useful scientific knowledge while having fun. Our main goal is to spark children's interest in space exploration and science.

Creativity & Design Factors

The creativity of our project lies in seamlessly blending gaming with education through interactive, real-world-inspired missions. While designing this beta version, our team carefully considered the target audience's age (7–14 years old). We kept the controls simple and intuitive while using engaging graphics to ensure the game remains visually appealing and exciting for children.
